cases.sentence: Когда Анна вошла в комнату, Долли сидела в маленькой гостиной с белоголовым ___, уж теперь похожим на отца, и слушала его урок из французского чтения.
cases.explain: «пухлым мальчиком» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: When Anna went into the room, Dolly was sitting in the little drawing-room with a white-headed fat little boy, already like his father, giving him a lesson in French reading. As the boy read, he kept twisting and trying to tear off a button that was nearly off his jacket. His mother had several times taken his hand from it, but the fat little hand went back to the button again. His mother pulled the button off and put it in her pocket.

cases.sentence: Правда, сколько она могла запомнить свое впечатление в Петербурге у Карениных, ей не нравился ___ их; что-то было фальшивое во всем складе их семейного быта.
cases.explain: «самый дом» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Dolly was crushed by her sorrow, utterly swallowed up by it. Still she did not forget that Anna, her sister-in-law, was the wife of one of the most important personages in Petersburg, and was a Petersburg grande dame. And, thanks to this circumstance, she did not carry out her threat to her husband—that is to say, she remembered that her sister-in-law was coming. “And, after all, Anna is in no wise to blame,” thought Dolly. “I know nothing of her except the very best, and I have seen nothing but kindness and affection from her towards myself.” It was true that as far as she could recall her impressions at Petersburg at the Karenins’, she did not like their household itself; there was something artificial in the whole framework of their family life. “But why should I not receive her? If only she doesn’t take it into her head to console me!” thought Dolly. “All consolation and counsel and Christian forgiveness, all that I have thought over a thousand times, and it’s all no use.”

cases.sentence: Услыхав шум платья и легких шагов уже в дверях, она оглянулась, и на ___ ее невольно выразилось не радость, а удивление.
cases.explain: «измученном лице» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Catching a sound of skirts and light steps at the door, she looked round, and her careworn face unconsciously expressed not gladness, but wonder. She got up and embraced her sister-in-law.

cases.sentence: Она взяла ее на руки и поцеловала. – ___, прелесть!
cases.explain: «Прелестная девочка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I? … Yes,” said Anna. “Merciful heavens, Tanya! You’re the same age as my Seryozha,” she added, addressing the little girl as she ran in. She took her in her arms and kissed her. “Delightful child, delightful! Show me them all.”

cases.sentence: Она ждала теперь ___; но Анна ничего такого не сказала.
cases.explain: «притворно-сочувственных фраз» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Dolly looked coldly at Anna; she was waiting now for phrases of conventional sympathy, but Anna said nothing of the sort.

cases.sentence: Из-за ___ ее блестящих глаз вдруг показались слезы.
cases.explain: «густых ресниц» — after the preposition «из-за», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Under the thick lashes of her shining eyes tears suddenly glittered. She moved nearer to her sister-in-law and took her hand in her vigorous little hand. Dolly did not shrink away, but her face did not lose its frigid expression. She said:

cases.sentence: Как лучше поступить в этом ___? – вот о чем надо подумать.
cases.explain: «ужасном положении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “But, Dolly, what’s to be done, what’s to be done? How is it best to act in this awful position—that’s what you must think of.”

cases.sentence: – Я одно скажу, – начала Анна, – я его сестра, я знаю его характер, эту способность все, все забыть (она сделала жест пред лбом), эту способность ___, но зато и полного раскаяния.
cases.explain: «полного увлечения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “One thing I would say,” began Anna. “I am his sister, I know his character, that faculty of forgetting everything, everything” (she waved her hand before her forehead), “that faculty for being completely carried away, but for completely repenting too. He cannot believe it, he cannot comprehend now how he can have acted as he did.”

cases.sentence: Ведь мы смеялись, бывало, над ним, что он к каждому слову прибавлял: – «Долли ___».
cases.explain: «удивительная женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Dolly, hush, darling. I saw Stiva when he was in love with you. I remember the time when he came to me and cried, talking of you, and all the poetry and loftiness of his feeling for you, and I know that the longer he has lived with you the loftier you have been in his eyes. You know we have sometimes laughed at him for putting in at every word: ‘Dolly’s a marvelous woman.’ You have always been a divinity for him, and you are that still, and this has not been an infidelity of the heart. …”

cases.sentence: Нет, могу, – сказала Анна, подумав; и, уловив мыслью положение и свесив его на ___, прибавила: – Нет, могу, могу, могу.
cases.explain: «внутренних весах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I don’t know, I can’t judge. … Yes, I can,” said Anna, thinking a moment; and grasping the position in her thought and weighing it in her inner balance, she added: “Yes, I can, I can, I can. Yes, I could forgive it. I could not be the same, no; but I could forgive it, and forgive it as though it had never been, never been at all. …”
